long_biography.plain_text:
Hompes launched Scotch & Soda at 24 as a wholesale menswear label rather than a retail chain. Its practical, colourful sports jackets gave the young Amsterdam business a distinct position and won customers in neighbouring European markets. The brand's first fifteen years remained centred on men's clothing sold through other retailers.

In 2000, Eric Bijlsma, Joep Krouwels and Patrick Munsters acquired nearly four-fifths of the company while Hompes kept a 21.8 percent holding. The incoming partners repositioned the label and introduced company stores, women's and children's lines, and a much larger international network. Hompes's remaining interest was part of the ownership sold to Kellwood and Sun Capital in 2011.

In 2000, Eric Bijlsma, Joep Krouwels and Patrick Munsters acquired nearly four-fifths of the company while Hompes kept a 21.8 percent holding.
